evals.name: first-simulation-from-scratch
evals.prompt: I need to load test our local API. Set up a Gatling load testing project from scratch in a folder called load-tests/ — TypeScript. One simulation that hits GET http://localhost:3001/v1/products, ramps up to a steady rate, and fails the run if more than 1% of requests error out. Tell me the exact command to run it and what I need installed first.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Gatling JS project: package.json with @gatling.io/core+http+cli, tsconfig, a *.gatling.ts simulation using injectOpen with a ramp then constant rate, assertions on success rate, named requests, and the npx gatling run command. Prerequisites should be Node+npm only — NOT a JDK.

evals.name: auth-correlation-and-unique-data
evals.prompt: Write a Gatling simulation that registers a new user then logs in and fetches their profile. Each virtual user needs a unique email or registration will collide, and the profile call needs the JWT the login returns. Base URL comes from an env var.
evals.expected_output: A simulation using a session function or feeder for unique per-user data, check(...).saveAs to capture the token from the login response, and a function-based Authorization header reading it back from the session.

evals.name: community-edition-boundary
evals.prompt: We're on the free version of Gatling. I want to run our load test across several machines to generate more traffic, and see the results trending over time in a dashboard. How do I set that up?
evals.expected_output: Should state plainly that distributed/multi-injector runs and hosted trend dashboards are Gatling Enterprise Edition features, not available in Community, rather than inventing a way to do it. Should offer what IS possible locally (single-machine runs, the local HTML report).
